item.text:
The cache contains only `v1.7.3` (no other version to diff against as a bug oracle), confirming there is no additional automated way to surface defects beyond the direct source review and tests already done.

The audit is substantively complete. Consolidated result (full detail in [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-11_16-25-33-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/report.md)):

- **Provenance:** the graded implementation is the unmodified upstream `github.com/hashicorp/raft v1.7.3` — verified byte-for-byte against the module artifact, an independent re-extraction of the Go-trusted zip, and the signed checksum-database record. No injected defect exists in the graded module.
- **Consensus implementation:** no concrete correctness defect demonstrated. Six full-package runs plus a full `-race` run pass; no membership/snapshot/transport/commitment test fails.
- **C1 (confirmed, reproduced):** the shipped test helper `cluster.EnsureSamePeers` (`testing.go:691`) samples `rafts[0]`'s configuration once and never refreshes it, so a transient lag becomes a guaranteed 5s spurious failure (18/100 runs of `TestRaft_HasExistingState`); re-sampling inside the retry loop yields 100/100. This is a test-utility bug, not a consensus-correctness bug. Scratch reproduction and traces are preserved under `work/diag/`, with raw logs under the run's retained `executions/…`.
- **Scope limits:** nested `fuzzy/`/`raft-compat/` modules are outside the graded package and unbuildable offline (dependency zips absent, read-only module cache, unchecked-out submodule); they can only be inspected, not executed.

No blockers. Further turns would be diminishing-returns source reading; if the runner prefers, the audit can be considered complete with the report as the deliverable.
